subject: ss-radiology
title: Pulmonary tuberculosis: pathogenesis, forms and diagnosis

steps.tx: **Mycobacterium tuberculosis** is an aerobic **acid-fast bacillus** whose waxy, mycolic-acid-rich wall resists staining and limits drug entry. Transmission occurs through airborne droplet nuclei from a person with infectious pulmonary or laryngeal disease. Cavitary cases are the most infectious, shedding very high bacillary loads into sputum.

steps.tx: Inhaled bacilli are engulfed by **alveolar macrophages**, which fail to fuse the phagosome with lysosomes, so the organism replicates. Around two to four weeks, **cell-mediated immunity** (CD4 T cells releasing interferon-gamma) forms granulomas with central caseous necrosis. Only about 10 percent of immunocompetent infected people develop active disease in their lifetime.

steps.tx: Pulmonary TB is split into **primary** disease, seen in middle or lower zones and common in children, and **postprimary (adult-type)** disease, typically apical or posterior upper-lobe cavitation. In HIV with CD4 below 200 per microlitre, the picture shifts to a primary-like pattern with diffuse infiltrates, little cavitation, effusion and intrathoracic adenopathy.

steps.tx: Confirm before treating. **Xpert MTB/RIF** is the WHO first-line test: it detects **Mycobacterium tuberculosis** and **rifampicin** resistance in under two hours, with about 85 percent pulmonary sensitivity and 98 percent specificity. **Sputum smear microscopy** alone cannot tell tuberculosis apart from other mycobacteria, so empirical **antitubercular therapy** should usually wait for microbiological proof.

steps.tx: Tuberculin skin test and **interferon-gamma release assays** such as QuantiFERON or T-SPOT detect infection, not active disease, and cannot predict who will progress. Non-tuberculous mycobacteria, lung cancer and chronic aspergilloma mimic TB, so a persistent upper-lobe cavity should prompt bronchoscopy or biopsy and cultures before labelling it TB.

steps.tx: Classify resistance, because it changes the regimen. **MDR-TB** means resistance to at least isoniazid and the other core first-line agent. **Pre-XDR-TB** adds fluoroquinolone resistance, while **XDR-TB** adds resistance to another group A agent, for example bedaquiline or linezolid. Smear-positive cavitary disease is the most infectious form and needs prompt action.

steps.tx: Untreated TB is often fatal, but timely drug-susceptible treatment cures most patients. Survivors may keep **post-TB lung disease**: airflow obstruction, bronchiectasis, pulmonary hypertension and residual cavities that can later host an aspergilloma. Ensure treatment completion and check for HIV, since antiretroviral timing and drug interactions matter.
